wire.settings.asks.description.note: Says the setting applies immediately everywhere (terminal UI, desktop app, phone). Do not imply a restart.

wire.settings.asks.title.note: Section heading for the queued-question settings. 'Ask' is the product noun for a question an agent queues for the user; keep it short and consistent with the ask bar/list vocabulary.

wire.settings.asks_lapsed_visible_for.ch.note: Measured from the ask's deadline, not from when it was asked.
A duration; use the locale's natural form for one hour.
A duration of 24 hours (not 'one day'): the four choices read as a ladder.
Measured from the ask's deadline; '(default)' marks the shipped value, keep it.
The ask disappears the moment its deadline passes.

wire.settings.asks_lapsed_visible_for.he.note: Shown as '<help> · default: 7d' on the settings page's 74-cell detail line at 80 columns; keep the help within 58 cells so the default clause fits. Display only: hiding never answers or deletes the ask.

wire.settings.asks_lapsed_visible_for.la.note: Row label; 29 cells is the settings page's label budget (_LABEL_BUDGET). 'Timed-out' = the ask's deadline passed with no answer. The row only changes how long such an ask stays SHOWN; it does not change whether the agent hears a late answer.

wire.settings.display_composer_command.h.note: The value is a shell command; the terminal UI runs it on a timer and shows the first line of its standard output as a segment of the status band (the row under the input). 'the band' = that status band, as in the sibling 'Band: …' rows. The settings page's detail box is 54 cells at 60 columns, so keep it within 54.

wire.settings.display_composer_command.l.note: 'Band' is the status row under the input, as in the sibling 'Band: …' rows; keep that prefix consistent with them. 'Status command' is a shell command the user writes.

wire.settings.display_composer_command.p.note: An example file path, shown faint in the empty editor. Do not translate: it is a path.

wire.settings.display_composer_command_i.note: The unit is seconds; 5-3600 is the accepted range and must stay as digits.
How often the status command reruns. Same 'Band:' prefix as the sibling rows.

wire.settings.guardrails.description.note: One line under the section heading. 'Dangerous' means destructive, e.g. deleting important files. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.guardrails.title.note: Section heading on the settings page. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.guardrails_critical_overri.note: Explains a safety override. Must keep both facts: OFF refuses critical deletions outright; ON sends them to an automatic safety check (never lets them through unchecked). 'From this machine's settings' = the settings page or CLI in the same process; a file edit (including by the agent) does not count. No ICU arguments.
wire.settings.guardrails_critical_overri.role: Settings row help for the guardrails section in the TUI and connected settings UI

wire.settings.guardrails_critical_overri.note: Label fits the 29-cell label budget. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.guardrails_enabled.help.note: User guardrail rules are markdown files the user writes; the built-in dangerous-delete check is not switchable. 'dangerous-delete' is a rule identifier and stays untranslated. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.guardrails_enabled.label.note: Label fits the 29-cell label budget. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.guardrails_judge_timeout_s.note: The safety check is an automatic model review of a risky tool call. Fail-closed: no answer means blocked. No ICU arguments.
Label fits the 29-cell label budget; '(s)' is seconds. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.guardrails_rules_dir.help.note: '*.md' is a literal file pattern and stays untranslated. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.guardrails_rules_dir.label.note: Label fits the 29-cell label budget. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.providers_anthropic_subage.note: Explains the threshold for delegated (subagent) requests only. '5 minutes' and '1-hour' are Anthropic's two prompt-cache lifetimes; keep both durations. 0 is the default and means no SIZE rule only: the separate after-a-4-minute-call rule stays on unless the main 1-hour setting is 0. '4 minutes' is the fixed 240-second threshold; keep the number.

Row label within the settings page's 29-cell label budget; the value is a token count. 'Subagent' is a delegated child agent; '1h' is the one-hour prompt-cache lifetime. Sibling of 'Anthropic 1h cache above (tokens)'.

wire.settings.remote_compute.description.note: Desktop-only section header sentence. Must say the feature is a PREVIEW and that work runs on Radient-hosted compute. 'Mesh network' is the product term for the user's device network; do not translate it as a social network or a Wi-Fi network.

wire.settings.remote_compute.title.note: Section heading for the remote-compute preview. 'Compute' is the product noun for where a run executes; keep it short enough for the settings header's 34-cell value column.

wire.settings.remote_compute_enabled.cho.note: What OFF means: work stays on this machine. Lowercase, about 10 cells.
What ON means: remote runs are allowed. Lowercase, about 20 cells.

wire.settings.remote_compute_enabled.hel.note: Must state this is a preview, that it sends the user's work to Radient-hosted compute, and that the run is bound to ONE of the user's mesh networks — the tenant claim. The old wording said 'in your mesh network', which read as containment and is not what the slice enforces. 'Radient' is a product name: keep it unchanged. Keep near 67 cells (en is 66; the 80x24 detail line sheds longer copy, so stay within 74).

wire.settings.remote_compute_enabled.lab.note: Boolean row label under the Remote compute section. Keep under 29 cells.

wire.settings.session_cleanup_temporary_.note: Explains the idle window for temporary chats. Do not imply that normal chats are affected.
A 'temporary chat' is a conversation that is not kept: it is left out of history and deleted automatically once idle for this long. Followed by a duration choice.

wire.settings.session_compression.descri.note: Desktop-only section header sentence. Must make clear that NOTHING is removed and that history stays complete: this section sits beside two cleanup sections and must not read as a third deletion policy.

wire.settings.session_compression.title.note: Section heading for transcript compression, a third storage control beside the two cleanup sections. Keep it short enough for the settings header's 34-cell value column.

wire.settings.session_compression_after_.note: Carries both bounds and the default because the page paints help but not min/max. 'Idle' is measured from the transcript's last write, not from when the session was created.
Sub-row label with the page's '↳' prefix, within the 29-cell budget. Names the threshold in DAYS; the stored value is always days.

wire.settings.session_compression_enable.note: What OFF means: transcripts stay plain files, and sessions already compressed stay readable (the switch only stops new compressions).
What ON means, lowercase, in the terms of the age row directly below it.

Leads with what OFF means (nothing new is compressed, and already-compressed sessions are still readable) then what ON does, in the cleanup master's shape. The age row below carries the threshold; reads decompress automatically and the section description says so, so this line stays inside the settings page's ~100-cell help budget.
Row label within the settings page's 29-cell label budget (_LABEL_BUDGET). Boolean master switch: ON compresses transcripts older than the age row below.

wire.settings.session_scratchpad.descrip.note: Says the cap applies to each session's own scratch area and is checked per write, not at launch. Do not imply a restart.

wire.settings.session_scratchpad.title.note: Section heading for the scratchpad size cap. 'Scratchpad' is the product noun for a session's own scratch area (scratchpad://); keep it one word.

wire.settings.session_scratchpad_max_byt.note: Carries both bounds and the default because the page paints help but not min/max. Units are bytes; use the binary prefixes MiB/GiB, not MB/GB.

Row label; 29 cells is the settings page's label budget. It names the MAXIMUM bytes one session's scratchpad may hold (not the current size) and carries the unit because the desktop collapses help behind a disclosure (design D1). Every locale must fit the same 29-cell budget.

wire.settings.team_bridge_screening_ambi.note: The point of the sentence is ORDER, not arithmetic: this slice is taken OUT of the unaddressed ceiling (only part of the account's total), and the account total is named only as the thing it is never ADDED to, so raising this slice never raises the total. Keep 'carved out of, never added to' as the shape of that claim even if the idiom changes. No numbers: do not transliterate a default. No ICU arguments.

'Chatter' is unsolicited agent-to-agent background talk in a shared room, the cheapest thing to leave unscreened when the hour is spent; keep the informal-but-clear register. 'Ceiling per hour' as in the sibling rows. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.team_bridge_screening_budg.note: The whole sentence is the account-wide ceiling and says an edit applies at once with no restart. 'Rolling hour' means the last 60 minutes at any moment, not a clock hour; render it as the locale's natural phrase for a sliding one-hour window. Do NOT add, drop or restate the numeric default: the number lives in the app's own registry and must not be transliterated into this copy, so a later adjustment cannot leave a stale figure in a translation. 'Account' is the user's organization account, shared by every session and machine signed in to it. No ICU arguments.

A CEILING is a maximum the feature may spend, not a target. It counts SCREENING calls — the automatic safety check a message passes before an agent sees it — over a ROLLING hour (a window that slides: the last 60 minutes at any moment), per account. Keep it a ceiling on spend, never a quota to fill. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.team_bridge_screening_mode.note: Three claims to preserve. (1) The choice is tried FIRST, so it RE-ORDERS the tested list (Sonnet first, then Opus) and never narrows it. (2) Empty means the tested order, which is the safest default — say that, because an unset row is a real recommendation, not a missing value. (3) A choice can never block delivery: if the chosen model is unavailable or out of quota, this machine's own configured model and its fallbacks still screen. Do not transliterate model ids or numbers into this copy. No ICU arguments.

WHICH model performs the automatic safety check a message passes before an agent sees it — never whether the check runs, which is not optional. Not a strictness level and not a 'screen messages' switch: the value is a model name, and the help carries the fall-through promise. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.team_bridge_screening_send.note: Two claims to preserve: one sender's share defaults to HALF the account ceiling ('half' is a ratio, so it may be expressed in the locale's own words, but it is not a number to transliterate), and no sender can ever exceed the account ceiling itself — the share is capped by the total, so one busy sender cannot monopolise the hour. No ICU arguments.

'Sender' is one other member or one of their agents in the organization; this ceiling limits a SINGLE sender's share of the account's hour. Keep 'per-sender' as the compact form of that. No ICU arguments.

wire.settings.team_bridge_screening_unad.note: Same carved-out-of-the-ceiling claim as the ambient sibling: a slice of the account total, never an addition. 'A person addressing your agent' is a human writing to the agent directly (a DM or an @mention) — the messages the remaining slice is reserved for. No numbers: do not transliterate a default. No ICU arguments.

'Unaddressed' means a message NOT addressed to the user's own agent — chatter in a room, or an agent mentioning it in passing — as opposed to a person writing to it directly. Keep the label short; the help carries the definition. No ICU arguments.
